## Objective
- Build a playable modern Australian trade strategy game inspired by Squatter, with trade, climate, policy, events, AI opponents, and mobile controls.

## Requirements
- The original request called for real-time import/export data, solo AI difficulty levels, online modes and lobbies, animated dice, music/sound/voices/weather, and touchscreen controls.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at finish.

## Decisions
- Built a standalone browser game with solo AI and local pass-and-play; online matchmaking is not implemented without a server.
- Use fictionalized market values and shifts, not live economic data; the in-game guide discloses these are not forecasts.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the responsive game UI, 20-space trade board, AI difficulty options, pass-and-play mode, market and policy actions, events, weather, investment, scoring, generated sound effects, and mobile action buttons.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Opened the trade desk in Playwright and confirmed the board, player ledger, market ticker, and dashboard render.

### Active
- Interactive verification remains incomplete: market/policy actions, dice roll, tile resolution, AI progression, and mobile layout have not been tested.
- Changes are uncommitted.

### Blocked
- Real online matchmaking/lobbies, live trade data, full music, and voice acting require backend/data/audio resources not present in the project.

## Next Move
1. Test the market and policy actions, dice roll, tile resolution, and AI turn progression in Playwright.
2. Check mobile layout and look for additional console errors; fix gameplay or UI issues found.
3. Optionally add a favicon or otherwise resolve the known `/favicon.ico` 404, then report assumptions and online-mode limitation.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and controls.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual design and board/counter styling.
- `game.js`: Game logic, AI, events, economy, sound, and interactions.

## Important Context
- Local testing URL: `http://localhost:3002`; server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.

- Build a playable modern Australian trade strategy game inspired by Squatter, with trade, climate, policy, events, AI opponents, and mobile controls.

- Original scope included live import/export data, solo AI difficulty levels, online modes and lobbies, animated dice, music/sound/voices/weather, and touchscreen controls.

## Objective
- Build a playable modern Australian trade strategy game inspired by Squatter, featuring trade, climate, policy, events, AI opponents, and mobile controls.

## Requirements
- Original scope included live import/export data, solo AI difficulty levels, online modes and lobbies, animated dice, music/sound/voices/weather, and touchscreen controls.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at finish.

## Decisions
- Built a standalone browser game with solo AI and local pass-and-play; online matchmaking is not implemented without a server.
- Use fictionalized market values and shifts, not live economic data; the in-game guide discloses these are not forecasts.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created responsive game UI, 20-space trade board, AI difficulty options, pass-and-play mode, market and policy actions, events, weather, investment, scoring, generated sound effects, and mobile action buttons.

- Finish mobile interaction checks if needed.

### Blocked
- Real online matchmaking/lobbies, live trade data, full music, and voice acting require backend/data/audio resources not present in the project.

## Next Move
1. Reload `http://localhost:3002` and verify the favicon loads without console errors.
2. Optionally verify the mobile policy/roll buttons, then report assumptions and the online-mode limitation.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, AI, events, economy, sound, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game screens and controls; favicon link.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and board styling.
- `favicon.svg`: Newly added game favicon.
